meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (num).

examples.text: 너희는 사람이 몇인데 그걸 아무도 못 봤냐?
examples.trans: With so many staffers on your team, how did nobody catch that?
Here the word for 'so many, yet' is key.

meanings.note: Bound counter noun used with native Korean numbers (한 시, 두 시, 세 시, 네 시).

examples.trans: What time is it now?
The meeting starts at three o'clock.

meanings.note: Slightly more formal/deferential variant of 네, commonly used when speaking to a boss or superior.

examples.trans: Yes, understood.
Yes, I will prepare it right away.
I want to stayed up all night right now.
How about trying to stayed up all night together tomorrow?

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.

examples.text: 피디가 마지막 순간까지 잊지 않아야 되는 게 뭔지 알아?
examples.trans: Do you know what a producer must never forget until the very last moment?
The topic of until the moment came up during this shoot.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

examples.text: 이 순간이 왔다! 필연적 선택, 피할 수는 없다, 된장찌개!
examples.trans: The moment has arrived! An inevitable choice you cannot escape—soybean-paste stew!
The topic of inevitable came up in today's meeting.

examples.text: 여기서 선택을 못 받아서 낙오되신 분들은 신입 피디와 함께 갑니다.
examples.trans: Anyone not chosen here and left behind will travel with our rookie producer.
The topic of choice, selection came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 너 왜 내 눈 피해? 너 왜 거짓말해?
examples.trans: Why are you avoiding my eyes? Why are you lying to me?
This expression comes from 'are you avoiding?'.

meanings.note: Bound noun used in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 ('can / cannot').

examples.trans: I can read Korean.
I cannot go today.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

examples.text: 이 순간이 왔다! 필연적 선택, 피할 수는 없다, 된장찌개!
examples.trans: The moment has arrived! An inevitable choice you cannot escape—soybean-paste stew!
The topic of soybean-paste stew came up in today's meeting.
Did you hear about this the best!?
I was busy today because of the best!.

examples.text: 최고의 난제, 오늘 점심엔 뭐 먹지?
examples.trans: Humanity's greatest riddle: what should we eat for lunch today?
The topic of hardest riddle, dilemma came up in today's meeting.

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?

examples.text: 당연해 그건. 점심 먹어야지. 여기서 군만두 맛있어.
examples.trans: Of course you won't. Let's eat lunch. The fried dumplings here are delicious.
The topic of lunch came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Everyday verb for eating a meal or food; honorific equivalent is 드시다.

examples.trans: Let's eat lunch together.
Did you eat breakfast?

meanings.note: Kinship term used by females.

meanings.en: older male friend or colleague (used by a female)
meanings.note: Commonly used in Korea to address a close older male acquaintance or coworker.

examples.trans: I have one older brother.
Oppa, do you have time right now?

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun for something near the speaker; often contracted to 이거 in speech.

examples.trans: Did you film this too?
How much is this?

meanings.note: Used before time nouns like 이번 주 (this week)

examples.trans: There is a meeting this Friday.
I will definitely succeed this time.
Did you hear about this 1 night?
I was busy today because of 1 night.

examples.text: 전체적으로 재정비하자. 자막, 음악 이런 거 다시 한번 살펴보고 예고도 빵빵하게 하나 만들어서 붙이고.
examples.trans: Let us overhaul everything—recheck the captions and music, and cut a killer preview to air right after.
Why don't we let our youngest producer try cutting the preview?
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금

examples.text: 이번에 일박 예고를 좀 특이하게 만들어 보겠다고…
examples.trans: They said they wanted to make the show's preview extra unique this week…

examples.text: 너무 속상해하지 말고 이번 회 한번 끝내주게 뽑아봐! 너희 예고도 특이하다고 화제가 좀 되던데.
examples.trans: Do not feel too down—cut an awesome episode this week! People are already buzzing that your preview was unique.
I want to making right now.
How about trying to making together tomorrow?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

meanings.note: adjective like this

examples.trans: This kind of thing.
It is like this.

meanings.note: Used as broadcasting loanword (멘트).

examples.text: 방송으로 치면 클로징 다 마치고 스크롤 올라가는데 멘트 다시 시작하는 상황 아니겠습니까?
examples.trans: In broadcasting terms, is this not like restarting the host's monologue while the closing credits are already rolling?!
This point about spoken commentary is really important.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: interrogative pronoun; becomes 누가 before subject particle -가
indefinite pronoun

examples.trans: Did someone come outside?
Who is that person?

meanings.note: Irregular ㅡ-stem verb: 쓰다 + -어 becomes 써.
Commonly used for tools, money, or time.

examples.trans: I write in my diary every night.
I wrote my name on the very first page of the book.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean term.

examples.trans: Since it's raining, please use an umbrella.
I lost my umbrella.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: When used with 알다/모르다, it means knowing or not knowing a fact or how to do something.

examples.trans: I knew it would rain.
Do you know how to swim?

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 암튼 나 이번에 감이 무지 좋아!
examples.trans: Anyway, my gut feeling about this premiere is seriously great!
Here the word for 'gut feeling, intuition' is key.

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.

examples.text: 그 우산 피디는 할 줄 아는 게 뭐야? 감도 없어, 사람 비위도 못 맞춰!
examples.trans: What does that Umbrella PD even know how to do?! He has zero sense and cannot flatter anyone!
The topic of someone's mood / favor even came up in today's meeting.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.
I want to because we cannot match right now.
How about trying to because we cannot match together tomorrow?

meanings.en: a lot, much, in large quantity
meanings.note: Adverbial form of 많다 (to be many/much)

examples.trans: I did a lot of work today.
Please eat plenty and enjoy.

meanings.note: Describes something unusual or out of the ordinary.
Used when sensing something is wrong.

examples.trans: The computer sounds a bit strange.
It's suspicious that he's suddenly being so nice.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: Contracted form of 이야기하다

examples.trans: Let's talk again later.
Please tell me honestly.

meanings.note: Used as casual imperative (대봐!).

examples.text: 골라도 비싼 애기를 골랐어! 이 치사한 놈 진짜, 이거 손만 대봐!
examples.trans: Out of all of them, he picked an expensive baby! You petty jerk—just dare lay a finger on it!
Let us do that (just dare touch) right away.

examples.text: 아니 무슨 비밀번호를 이렇게 바꿔 놨냐?
examples.trans: Wait, why did you change the door code like this?

examples.text: 나는 빵빵빵빵이 좋은데 네가 바꾼 거 아냐.
examples.trans: I liked four zeros, you were the one who changed it.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (det).

examples.text: 정권 바뀌면 바꿀 게 한두 가지가 아니에요.
examples.trans: When leadership changes, there is way more than one or two things you have to change.
Here the word for 'one or two' is key.

meanings.note: General-purpose counter noun used with native Korean determiners (한 개, 두 개, 세 개).

examples.trans: How many do you need?
I bought three loaves of bread.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.

확실하다.gloss: to be certain, to be clear

meanings.en: to be certain, to be sure, to be clear
meanings.note: Sino-Korean adjective.

examples.trans: Are you sure?
clear evidence

meanings.en: to joke, to kid, to play a prank
meanings.note: 장난해? is a very common casual expression meaning 'Are you kidding me?'.

examples.trans: Are you kidding me right now?
Please don't joke around.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.
